Traditional wedding vows often include a pledge to honor our husband. What does honoring actually mean and are we (am I) really doing it?

Honor: To reverence; manifest the highest veneration for, in words and actions; to entertain the most exalted thought of; worship; to adore. (Webstersdictionary.com)

Looking back it's clear that honoring my husband was much easier in the early years of marriage. Over time, slights (perceived or actual), annoyances, hurt feelings, feelings of being taken for granted...all these things and more seem to just add up and create an entirely new monster which is resentment. Ugly, mean ole nasty resentment, once established, is a really difficult thing to love through. Resentment has a way of cutting off all the good things one has to offer and in essence, makes someone an emotional island. It leads to withholding as a means to punish our spouse and is cancer to ourselves as well as our marriage. Resentment needs to be dismantled using a forgiving spirit, love, and a dash of humility.

There are quite a few ways to start honoring our husband once again...the way we promised we would when we said our vows. Does he make requests that seem trivial to you and are therefore ignored? My husband likes fresh sheets, a made bed and his laundry folded and put away. When I ignore these minor requests (which happens sometimes) I'm essentially telling him that his needs aren't important to me. Honoring my husband through actions is an area where I need some work.

We also honor our husband through thoughts and words. When we see our husbands do something helpful, cool, or just awesome say so and let him know you noticed. It matters and I don't do this nearly enough. Sometimes when I'm annoyed I won't verbally express it but on the inside I'm having a few words with him and telling him off...this isn't good and is also a form of dishonoring him. Am going to work on stopping myself when negative thoughts come in and try to reframe those thoughts as to not give them any power.

Communicating appreciation, love, and adoration through words, thoughts, and acts of service are a great way to begin restoring honor in marriage..the way we promised we would the day we married.
